[STYLE]
Create one polished educational illustration for elementary-school children, in a cute high-quality 3D animated-cartoon style: rounded forms, soft tactile materials, pastel colors, expressive friendly characters, natural soft lighting, gentle shadows. A warm contemporary storybook atmosphere, visibly three-dimensional, consistent artistic style across this five-image series. Wide landscape 16:9.

[SCENE DESCRIPTION]
A bright cozy family living room on a sunny afternoon. One child is reading while resting comfortably on the sofa; another child is sleeping beside them. Everyday furniture fits naturally into one unified room.

[TARGET VOCABULARY]
Exact eight labels: sofa, television, lamp, chair, table, read, sleep, comfortable.
sofa — noun, a sofa with visible seat, back and arms; television — noun, recognizable screen and stand; lamp — noun, a table lamp with shade and base; chair — noun, a separate single chair; table — noun, a low foreground table; read — verb, eyes focused on an open book; sleep — verb, closed eyes and relaxed resting posture; comfortable — adjective, the reading child looks at ease, shoulders and legs relaxed against a thick seat.

[OBJECT VISIBILITY RULES]
Show the whole sofa silhouette, the standalone chair and its legs, and the table top and legs. Television screen is blank. Keep the lamp unobstructed. Both children and the open book remain clear. Do not label background cushions or rugs.

[COMPOSITION]
Television on the left, sofa centrally in the midground, lamp on a small side table to the right. Main target table in the foreground center and a standalone chair foreground right, separated from the sofa. Leave air around the reading and sleeping children and distinct label spaces above and below the sofa.

[CHARACTERS / ACTIONS]
The reading child sits on the left portion of the sofa, looking down at an open book, loose shoulders and relaxed legs. The other child rests with eyes closed on the right portion. Do not give the reading child a sleeping expression. comfortable arrow ends near the relaxed shoulder/posture; read arrow ends at the book-reading action; sleep arrow ends near the sleeping child’s head. Each furniture arrow ends at the named furniture.

[ANNOTATION STYLE]
Overlay thin white casual hand-drawn single-stroke pen lines and lowercase handwritten English labels. Slightly imperfect, relaxed and stylish, but crisp and easy to read. One short curved arrow per label with an unmistakable endpoint. Reserve medium-toned quiet areas for strong contrast with white text. Use a subtle darker halo only where necessary for legibility. Arrange labels in open spaces near their referents, never over faces, key objects or action details. Keep lines separated; no tangled arrows.

[TEXT RULES]
Render exactly eight vocabulary labels, each once, with exact spelling as listed above. All labels lowercase, readable at normal image size. No title, subtitles, definitions, translations, narrative, signage, brand names, letters on props, numbers, speech bubbles or any other text. The listed senses are instructions for depiction, not text to print.

[DECORATION]
At most two tiny white hand-drawn sparkles or hearts in empty peripheral space. Preserve generous breathing room; no additional text doodles.

[NEGATIVE REQUIREMENTS]
Avoid inventory-catalog arrangements, isolated object panels, clutter, tiny target objects, obscured objects, crowded labels, crossing arrows, misspellings, duplicate labels, photorealism, flat 2D art, dark dramatic lighting, extra limbs or malformed hands. No interface controls, cards, borders, logos, watermarks, Chinese text or additional vocabulary labels.

[OBJECT VISIBILITY RULES]

Hoop and hanging net large and fully visible. Separate face, shooting arms and raised feet for different annotation endpoints. Team jerseys have no lettering or numbers.

Foreground shooter slightly left of center, whole body in view. Ball travels toward a hoop on the upper right with a clear net beneath. [SCENE DESCRIPTION]
A warm birthday party around a table. A birthday child leans toward a birthday cake and blows gently at its candle while friends clap in celebration. Gifts, a clean empty plate and a few separated balloons complete a cheerful lived-in party scene.

[TARGET VOCABULARY]

cake — noun, an unobscured birthday cake; candle — noun, one clearly upright candle on the cake; gift — noun, a wrapped present with a simple bow; balloon — noun, a round balloon in the background; plate — noun, an empty plate beside the cake; blow — verb, pursed lips directed toward the candle and a slightly leaning flame; celebrate — verb, friends clapping at the party; happy — adjective, a friend’s clear smiling expression.

[OBJECT VISIBILITY RULES]
Cake and gift must not be hidden by hands or arms. Candle is large enough to distinguish from cake and its flame remains visible. Empty plate has a recognizable rim and clear space around it. Balloons separate from each other. No birthday banner, printed wrapping, age numbers, cake text or clothing letters.

[COMPOSITION]
Cake centered on the table foreground, empty plate to its right and gift to its left with generous separation. Birthday child behind cake, face visible in three-quarter view. Two friends flank the child, clapping; one particularly clear happy smile. Few pastel balloons in the upper background. Quiet medium-toned wall and tabletop areas provide readable label positions.

[CHARACTERS / ACTIONS]
Birthday child purses lips toward candle, whose flame leans slightly away, making blow recognizable without text. Friends clap with hands away from cake and faces. celebrate arrow targets the clapping party action; happy targets one friend’s delighted expression; blow targets the visible mouth-to-candle action.
